full_judgment: 6. Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners has taken me to the judgments of both the courts below and other materials on record and submits that the court below failed to take notice that when a summon is returned stating that the process server served the summons affixing the copy under Rule 17, the court shall, if the return under that rule has riot been verified by affidavit of the serving officer, shall examine the serving officer on oath touching the proceedings or make such further inquiry in the matter but the courts below accepted the service without observing by those formalities although the requirements are mandatory in law and in spite of such position the courts below failed to advert to those materials on record arid committed error of law resulting in any error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Alam next submits that from the face of the summons it would be evident that the Nazir of the Cowl handed over the summons of the suit for service to the process server on 2.3.1991 and on the same date i.e. 2.3.199 I at 10 A. M. (Morning) the process server had shown to have served the summons which definitely indicates that there was a collusion between the process-server and the opposite parties and the return (report) of service is false and fraudulent which has been made so that the opposite parties being plaintiffs can get a walk- over but both the courts failed to notice those aspects of the case and passing the impugned order committed error of law which has occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Alam again submits that the courts below took wrong presumption that the petitioner knew about the suit earlier on the basis of the information ship, but in fact. the information ship was written and filed by the learned Advocate when t he petitioner requested the learned Advocate to ascertain the exact position of the suit and that shows there was non-application of judicial mind and as such on wrong findings passed the impugned order which is liable to be set aside and further submits that the petitioner only on 16.9.1991 came to know about the suit on receipt of the enveloped and he filed the miscellaneous case under order 9 rule 13 C.P.C. on 30.9.1991 but the findings of the cowls below are wrong to the effect that the case is barred by limitation which has occasioned failure of justice.
